messages:
Maya (product): Quick thread on the action bar for the chat playground. Trying to settle on behavior for streaming + action controls, token microcounter placement, and a lightweight prompt picker. I sketched three options in Figma: layered overlay, fixed bottom bar, and inline compact. Link: https://figma.com/s/playground-actionbar-samples

Jon (design): Inline compact looks nicest for desktop but worried about discoverability for regen. Overlay gives room for extra affordances (confirm, undo) but adds a modal feel. Thoughts on a small persistent hint (chevron) to open the prompt picker vs an always-visible pill?

Priya (eng): From an API and telemetry standpoint, fewer controls = fewer accidental calls. Prefer one persistent pill for action (Stop/Regenerate) + a tiny separate token chip. If we expose `regen` as a distinct action we should debounce it server-side for ~400ms to avoid accidental double calls.

Eli (a11y): A few accessibility rules: 1) any toggle must have an ARIA-pressed or role=switch and clear labels 2) if we use hover-reveals, ensure keyboard focus reveals same content 3) token counter needs a non-visual label: "Tokens: 123" via sr-only.

Jon (design): Proposal B (compromise): persistent compact bar anchored to bottom of input. Left: token chip (small, muted). Center: main action pill. Right: prompt icon that opens mini library. Action pill behavior: while streaming it shows a pulsating dot + "Stop"; when stopped it flips to "Regenerate" with a subtle transform. Long-press opens an options menu: "Stop & save", "Stop only", "Regenerate now".

Priya (eng): Long-press menu is fine but we need keyboard parity. Maybe press+Alt or context menu (Shift+F10) opens same menu. Also need to standardize events: `action: stop`, `action: regenerate`, `action: apply_prompt` with an optional `queue:true|false` field.

Maya (product): Microcopy brainstorming: for the menu item "Stop & save" -> "Stop and keep partial response" vs "Stop and discard"? Which reads clearer? Also for toast after applying prompt: should it say "Prompt applied" or "Input replaced"?

Eli (a11y): Use explicit language: "Stop and keep partial response" is clearer. For toasts, "Input updated from prompt" is clearer than "Prompt applied". Also toasts should be role=alert and dismissible with Escape.

Jon (design): Token chip copy: show used/limit but hide limit for anonymous users? Maybe show just "123" for logged-out demos and "123 / 4,096" for signed-in. Visual density: chip should be 28px height, monospaced number, low-contrast border.

Priya (eng): Backend will stream token counts via websocket field `session.tokens.used` and `session.model.context_size`. Example: { "tokens": 123, "context": 4096 }. We'll avoid sending more than one token update per 150ms to reduce churn.

Maya (product): Prompt picker: mini-sheet that appears above input, keyboard shortcut "." opens it (like command menu). Quick-apply should not immediately overwrite input unless user chooses "Apply and run". Defaults to "Apply" which replaces input but doesn't trigger generation. We want to avoid surprising runs.

Jon (design): UX for mobile: bottom sheet with large touch targets, keep token chip hidden behind a small toggle to save space. Use haptic feedback on apply/regenerate on mobile.

Priya (eng): Edge-case: user applies prompt mid-stream and clicks "Apply and run". We'll implement queueing: server receives `apply_prompt` with `run_after: immediate | queued`. If immediate and stream active, we'll return 409 unless client sets `force: true`. Prefer queueing to avoid complex partial states.

Deploy Bot: deploy preview: https://preview.redwood/dev/playground-bar/1773005555 (screenshot + console logs).

Maya (product): Action items: Jon to finalize mock with bottom-anchored compact bar + long-press menu visual, Eli to produce a short a11y checklist (ARIA roles, keyboard mappings, SR text), Priya to add websocket token rate-limits and event schema to the API doc. Back by EOD Friday. :pray:
